claims.title: Authorization codes can be sent to attacker-controlled prefix-matching redirect URIs
claims.description: An outside attacker can initiate authorization for `process:authorization-server` using a redirect URI under their control that begins with a partner's registered URI. The authorization server accepts prefix matches and `flow:entity:member>entity:partner-app>return-with-authorization-code` returns the member's authorization code to the redirect URI, allowing the attacker to elicit and read that credential. The code is valid for ten minutes; if the attacker can also complete the applicable client exchange, the disclosed code yields a bearer token usable on `flow:entity:partner-app>process:rewards-api>call-rewards-api` to read the member's balances and transactions.

quotes.text: the authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with it
An authorization code stays valid for ten minutes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must induce a member authorization and supply a URI that passes the stated prefix check, but the browser-to-partner return crosses from `boundary:member-devices` to `boundary:partner-servers`. Impact is medium because the disclosed authorization code is a short-lived credential that can lead to one member's token-authorized rewards data if the associated exchange can be completed.

mitigations.detail: Register and compare normalized redirect URIs as exact values; reject prefix, wildcard, and parser-ambiguous matches.

mitigations.summary: Bind the authorization response to the client session
mitigations.detail: Require and validate state, use PKCE for public clients, and bind each authorization code to its client and exact redirect URI.

claims.title: Partner applications can read member rewards data beyond their business need
claims.description: A legitimate but over-privileged `entity:partner-app` receives every scope and can use a member bearer token through `flow:entity:partner-app>process:rewards-api>call-rewards-api`. An honest-but-curious or compromised partner can abuse that grant to elicit balance reads, points transactions, and gift-card redemption-related data from `process:rewards-api`, even where those fields exceed the partner's stated purpose. The resulting PII and financial activity can be retained by the partner and used to profile the member or target subsequent fraud.

quotes.text: The team gives every partner app every scope, because working out which scopes each partner needs took too long.
A partner app calls the rewards API with a member's access token.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because every partner app is deliberately issued every scope and can call the internet-facing `process:rewards-api` across `crossing:flow:entity:partner-app>process:rewards-api>call-rewards-api`. Impact is medium because the exposed responses contain a member's `pii` and `financial` rewards activity, although the described request path is token-bound to an individual member.

mitigations.detail: Define per-partner scopes and consent text for only the endpoints and fields each integration needs; do not issue redeem or transaction-history access to display-only partners.
Authorize each requested resource and return only the balance or fields required for the approved partner function.

claims.title: Identity-database traffic may expose passwords and refresh tokens on the internal path
claims.description: `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` carries member accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker able to observe the internal authorization-server-to-database segment can intercept those credentials and PII. Refresh tokens or authorization artifacts recovered this way can then be used against `process:authorization-server` to obtain access tokens and reach the rewards API as the affected member.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unverified and the attacker first needs an internal on-path position; the flow is not a derived boundary crossing. Impact is high because the flow carries `credentials` and `pii`, including refresh tokens that can extend access beyond the observed exchange.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce authenticated encryption for the database connection
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` to TLS with database-server authentication, and restrict plaintext database listeners.
Store password hashes using a modern password hashing scheme, rotate refresh tokens, and bind refresh-token use to the intended client where feasible.

claims.title: Rewards ledger traffic may disclose member balances and transactions
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points` carries balances and points transactions while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport encryption is absent, an attacker with an internal on-path position can intercept financial records between `process:rewards-api` and `store:points-ledger`. The collected balance and transaction history enables profiling of members and can be correlated with externally obtained identity data for targeted fraud.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because both the protocol and transport protection are unknown and observing this intra-cloud path requires a prior on-path foothold. Impact is medium because `store:points-ledger` holds every member's `financial` balances and points transactions.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the rewards API to ledger hop
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`, validate the ledger peer, and disable unencrypted database endpoints.

mitigations.summary: Document and test the connection posture
mitigations.detail: Record the protocol, TLS version, certificate validation, and key-management configuration for the ledger connection and test that plaintext downgrade is rejected.

claims.title: API request logs may expose bearer tokens while being shipped to the log store
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` carries every request header, including bearer access tokens, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the log-shipping connection is not effectively encrypted, an attacker observing that path can intercept reusable bearer credentials as well as request PII and financial context. A recovered token can then be presented to `process:rewards-api` to read the member's rewards information until the token expires.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` of this internal log path are unknown and interception requires an on-path foothold. Impact is high because the flow explicitly carries bearer access tokens, which are reusable credentials, alongside `pii` and `financial` request data.

mitigations.detail: Require mutually authenticated TLS for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` and verify the log-store endpoint.
Redact Authorization and other credential-bearing headers at `process:rewards-api` before events are emitted; use request correlation identifiers rather than raw bearer tokens.

claims.title: Account-closure traffic may reveal member account information on an unverified internal connection
claims.description: `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` has unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit` while it carries account-closure information to `store:identity-database`. If the unresolved transport state means the connection is unencrypted, an internal on-path attacker can intercept closure events and associated member account information. This reveals sensitive account status that can be used to identify inactive or recently closed accounts for follow-on social engineering.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the connection details and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown and an attacker must first observe the internal path. Impact is medium because the flow concerns member account status in `store:identity-database`, which is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for support-console database access
mitigations.detail: Set a verified TLS configuration for `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts`, including peer validation and a prohibition on plaintext fallback.

claims.title: Identity-database copies may disclose member credentials and PII if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:identity-database` holds member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy such as a backup, snapshot, or decommissioned volume can read the contents without using the authorization server's application controls. Disclosed refresh tokens and authorization artifacts can then be used to request access tokens from `process:authorization-server`, extending the loss into members' rewards data.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the rewards API connects to the ledger, how the support console connects to the identity database, or how any of the three stores is protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:identity-database:encryption_at_rest`: acquiring a backup or snapshot is a prerequisite, but such a copy bypasses the live application path if encryption is absent. Impact is high because the store is tagged `credentials` and `pii` and contains refresh tokens and authorization artifacts for the member population.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the identity database and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual at-rest posture, then require managed-key encryption for `store:identity-database`, including backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.

mitigations.summary: Restrict storage export and key use
mitigations.detail: Separate backup/export permissions from application access and limit decrypt capability to narrowly scoped recovery roles.

claims.title: Points-ledger copies may expose all member balances if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:points-ledger` contains every member's balance and every points transaction, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the store is unencrypted at rest, an attacker holding a copied disk, snapshot, or backup can read the full ledger outside `process:rewards-api` and its bearer-token checks. The corpus-level transaction history can reveal members' spending and reward activity and support targeted fraud or profiling.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the rewards API connects to the ledger, how the support console connects to the identity database, or how any of the three stores is protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `encryption_at_rest` is unverified and a storage copy must be obtained, but that copy bypasses the API if encryption is absent. Impact is medium because `store:points-ledger` holds the financial balances and transaction history of every member.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt ledger storage and its copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for `store:points-ledger`, backups, snapshots, and replicas, with managed keys and restricted export permissions.
Use separate least-privilege roles for ledger administration, backup operations, and recovery, and audit snapshot creation and export.

claims.title: API log-store copies may reveal reusable bearer tokens if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:api-log-store` holds every rewards-API request header, including bearer access tokens, and its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the store or an operational copy is unencrypted, an attacker with a backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can recover tokens and PII without going through `process:rewards-api`. Those bearer tokens can be used against the API until expiration, turning a log-copy disclosure into access to members' balance and transaction data.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:api-log-store:encryption_at_rest`: a storage copy is required, but it bypasses live API controls if encryption is absent. Impact is high because the logged Authorization headers contain bearer access tokens, reusable `credentials` that reach the API's PII and financial operations.

mitigations.detail: Redact Authorization headers at `process:rewards-api` before writing `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log`; invalidate and rotate any tokens previously logged where possible.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and tightly control log-store copies
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption at rest for `store:api-log-store` and every backup or snapshot, with separate access controls and audit trails equivalent to those for the source API data.
